name: Eliakim
overview: Eliakim is a male figure known for his role as the overseer of the household of King Hezekiah. The Bible specifically identifies him in this capacity, highlighting his administrative position during Hezekiah's reign. Other personal details such as tribal affiliation or additional notes are not recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliakim means 'G-d establishes,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God's sustaining power. Additionally, he is referred to by the divine title 'My servant Eliakim,' which underscores his role as one appointed by YHVH to serve faithfully.
familyAndRelationships: Eliakim is explicitly identified as the son of Hilkiah, establishing his immediate family connection. He is also described as a servant of YHVH, indicating a spiritual relationship of obedience and service. Beyond these, Scripture does not record further family relationships for Eliakim.
scriptureSignificance: Eliakim's significance lies in his entrusted leadership over the household of Hezekiah, marking him as a key official in the administration of Judah during a critical period. His designation as 'My servant' by God in Isaiah further emphasizes his divinely sanctioned role and faithful service. Through these roles, Eliakim exemplifies obedience and responsibility under God's sovereign rule.
